body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The big story this Friday is the passing of Dolores Huerta, the civil rights and labor icon whose roots run deep through Delano and the fields of Kern County, and neighbors across the county are remembering her this morning. Outside, it's a mild fall day — 59 degrees at Meadows Field on the way to a high near 73, no weather alerts, and air quality sitting at a moderate 91. Here's what happened while you slept and what's ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

It was a busy night for officers and dispatchers across the city. The call that drew the most attention came at 9:26 p.m., when officers were sent to Kentucky Street and Bale in east Bakersfield for seven juveniles reported in the area, dispatch putting their age at 15. One of them was said to have a firearm and was last seen walking south toward the railroad tracks in a white jumpsuit, so officers searched the tracks and the surrounding streets for him.

Earlier in the evening, two people cut through a razor-wire fence and got into a business yard at 8:53 p.m. Units set a perimeter and brought in a police dog and an air unit, and one of the two was reported hurt getting over the wire. A hit-and-run crash at 8:34 p.m. left a person with moderate to major injuries, and the car that fled was described as a black Toyota sedan heading east. A call about a possible unreported stolen vehicle with a firearm on the seat brought an air unit and a police dog to a business yard in the 5800 block of South Union Avenue at 7:01 p.m., where a man was found hiding under a fifth-wheel trailer and one person was taken into custody.

Later, a pursuit was reported on Edison Highway at 11:40 p.m., past Sterling and then Fairfax, at speeds from 85 up to 120 mph, with an air unit launching to follow. Officers also responded to a man with a machete on a bicycle reported on Cedar Street in central Bakersfield at 11:45 p.m. and on Fillmore Street on foot a few minutes later. Other calls through the night included a juvenile reported suicidal and holding a knife on Beardsley Avenue at 8:37 p.m., a fight between roommates involving a sword on Haven Avenue at 9:13 p.m., and a woman reported armed with a brick on Country View Lane at 3:53 a.m. Medical crews were sent to East Brundage Lane for difficulty breathing and to the Navigation Center for a maternity call, and a commercial fire alarm at a plant on Lerdo Highway was canceled.

## Today's weather

It's 59 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, and the National Weather Service expects a high near 73 today with a low around 56 tonight — about as pleasant a late-October day as the valley gives us. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and no active fires to report. Air quality is 91, which lands in the moderate range, so those with sensitivities may want to keep that in mind for extended time outdoors. Otherwise, it's a good day to be out and about.

## Top stories

**Bakersfield police are asking for the public's help finding a man accused of stealing items from an unlocked vehicle, Bakersfield Now reports.** The department's request is a reminder as the weather cools and more of us are out on foot and in driveways: locked doors and valuables out of sight remain the simplest defense. Anyone with information should reach out to BPD directly rather than approach a suspect.

**According to 23ABC, a new study from the firm Chain Cohn Clark has identified Bakersfield's most dangerous intersections, with the area around 23rd, 24th and Chester Avenue topping the list at 34 documented crashes over more than a decade of data.** Rounding out the top ten are Beale and Niles, 34th and Q, Niles and Union, Panama and Union, H Street and Ming, Brundage and P, Baker and Niles, Beale and Monterey, and H and Planz. The study also found that the most collisions in 2025 happened between 3 and 6 p.m. — the afternoon commute. A firm representative told the station that narrowing some roadways has actually slowed traffic, but a Bakersfield police lieutenant said the department weighs speed, collision type and severity, not raw crash counts alone, and that speeding remains a leading factor. BPD has installed six new red-light cameras as part of its response.

**KGET 17 reports that a driver has died after crashing into a vehicle that was slowing for children crossing a street in northeast Bakersfield.** The department's account points to a familiar and painful pattern — a driver failing to slow where kids are present. We'll have more detail as the investigation develops.

**23ABC also brings us a warmer story: a Bakersfield photojournalist's decades of photographs of Dolores Huerta, showing a more personal side of the civil rights icon.** John Harte, long a photographer for the Bakersfield Californian, first met Huerta in April 1993 in Delano, at the funeral procession for Cesar Chavez, when he knelt to photograph her stepping out of her dress shoes and into tennis shoes to join the four-mile march. That image was overlooked among hundreds taken that day and only made the paper this week, 33 years later. Harte told the station what struck him most about Huerta was how regular and approachable she remained despite her fame.

**And KGET 17 shares how Kern County communities are reacting to Huerta's loss, with residents describing what she meant to them personally.** For a county whose fields and farmworker history are bound up in her organizing, the remembrances carry particular weight. A separate KGET piece notes that her legacy lives on through art and advocacy — a fitting note for a woman who spent her life turning conviction into action.

## Something good

Dagny's is celebrating 30 years of keeping Bakersfield caffeinated. Three decades at the same local coffee spot is a rare thing anywhere, and it's a milestone worth raising a mug to — generations of regulars, early shifts and long conversations have passed through those doors. Congratulations to the whole Dagny's crew.

And downtown businesses are teaming up for a donation drive to help women in need, 23ABC reports. Girls Girl Social Club and StreetFair have rallied four downtown spots — Twisted Coffee, The Mint, Jerry's Pizza and Guthrie's — to collect essentials for the Open Door Network. Twisted Coffee is offering 10 percent off to anyone who donates, and Guthrie's is gathering books, scrapbooks, crayons and art supplies to offer comfort and creativity. Coordinator Amy Luna said she wanted to create something that brings people together to help those who may be struggling.

## Coming up this week

It's a light week on the public calendar, but there are a few dates worth marking. The Bakersfield City Council meets twice on Wednesday, November 4 — first at 3:30 p.m. and again at 5:15 p.m. — so check the agenda for which session covers what you care about. Then on Thursday, November 5, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m. Both bodies meet at City Hall downtown, and agendas are posted ahead of time for anyone who wants to weigh in.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. Tonight, October 30, Elias Medina takes the stage. Journey USA plays the Fox on November 7, sharing the date with Texas Tornado Tradition. The Cults & Classics series continues with "Play Misty for Me" on November 9, and the Nutcracker! Magical Christmas Ballet arrives November 13. If you're planning ahead, season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are also on sale.

Have a good Friday, Bakersfield. Lock your cars, watch for the kids crossing on your commute home, and be kind to each other out there.
